message.content:
The number of mitochondria in a cell varies widely depending on the cell type and its energy demands. Typical ranges are:

| Cell type | Typical mitochondrial count |
|-----------|-----------------------------|
| Neurons (high energy demand) | ~200–500 per neuron |
| Muscle cells (especially cardiac) | ~300–800 per cell |
| Hepatocytes (liver) | ~50–200 per cell |
| Epithelial cells | ~10–50 per cell |
| Stem cells (low energy demand) | ~5–20 per cell |

These numbers are approximate averages; individual cells can have anywhere from a few dozen to several thousand mitochondria.
